# Investment Memo: CHTR — 15 November 2026

**Verdict**: BUY (speculative, starter size only) | Conviction: Medium
**Price Target**: $205 (+48% from current $138.39); haircut probability-weighted range $195–215
**Time Horizon**: 12–24 months (key waypoints: Q4'26 print 29-Jan-27; 2027 capex guide; C-band auction 27-Apr-27)

---

**Investment Thesis**

Charter is a genuinely cheap, genuinely broken, genuinely levered asset. The core broadband franchise is in structural decline — accelerating subscriber losses, falling ARPU, negative organic revenue — and carries ~$104B of net debt against a ~$20–22B market cap, making the equity a levered call option on stabilization. But the bear case is now priced: at ~4.8–5.4x EV/EBITDA with a ~23% FCF yield, the market capitalizes permanent decline, while three dated, verifiable catalysts (capex falling to ≤$11B in 2027, $2B opex cuts plus $1B+ Cox synergies, deleveraging toward 3.5x) offer a credible path to FCF nearly doubling. The discount is wide enough to buy a small piece; the leverage is high enough that the piece must be small.

---

**Key Findings by Domain**

- **Macro & Sector**: Sector rated UNATTRACTIVE — cable unlikely to grow broadband subs this decade; FWA (~3.6–3.8M adds/yr) and fiber compress units and ARPU. Charter has the peer group's best operating margin (24.4%, +320bp vs median) but is the only peer with negative 2025 revenue (−0.6%). Macro is the worst quadrant for this equity: 10Y at 5.13% and bear-steepening, Fed re-hiking (3.88%), CPI 3.82%, mortgages 7.11% freezing move-related connects. Strong growth is paradoxically *negative* for CHTR — the equity needs disinflation and lower long yields.
- **Geopolitical & Legal**: Geopolitical risk LOW (zero foreign revenue — cleanest in sector). The discount is political-regulatory: NY's $15/$20 rate-regulation precedent with copycat bills, FCC merger conditions (DEI rollback, onshoring) as recurring M&A tax, ACP subsidy-clawback tail (~$3B received; open FCC verification probe), and the Sandoval securities class action (MTD pending) plus likely new filings off the Q3'26 impairment. C-band auction 27-Apr-27 prices the Verizon-MVNO dependency.
- **Equity Fundamentals — Value**: BUY. Probability-weighted IV $230–240 (I haircut to ~$205 — the base case assumes the EBITDA inflection it should be testing). ~30% equity FCF yield, P/B 0.9x post-impairment. Narrow moat, actively narrowing — revenue per customer falling is the single most important fact. Management: competent operator, over-levered allocator (C+).
- **Equity Fundamentals — Growth**: SELL. Rule of 40 = 7.5. Subscriber losses accelerating: −120k → −172k → **−233k** (Q3'26). Beat rate 2/7; PT cuts across the Street ($101–150 cluster). Explicitly notes the bull case is a value argument, not growth; revisit only on two quarters of improving net adds plus confirmed capex discipline.
- **Quantitative Signals**: Composite 44/100 — Value 95 (cheapest in telecom on all three legs), Momentum 5, Low-Vol 3. The leverage multiplier is the whole story: 1% EBITDA move = ~6.1% equity move. Beta −0.12 is spurious (R²=0.0009); correlation to CMCSA is 0.74, to SPY −0.03. Note: the "+27.55% revision" tool output is a period-mismatch artifact — true revision breadth is uniformly negative.
- **Financial Risk**: HIGH. BB+/Ba1; net leverage 3.93x vs 3.5x target; FCF/interest only 1.2x (the metric to watch); tangible equity −$77B; Altman Z 0.60. Mitigants: 11.1-year WAL, no 2026–27 refi cliff, EBITDA/interest 4.55x, FCF inflecting up. A −20% revenue scenario produces no default but functionally wipes the equity.
- **Non-Financial Risk**: HIGH, governance-led. CFO departed 11 days after the Cox close — still interim; Cox-family chairman; $6.33B impairment one quarter after paying $34.5B; May-26 ShinyHunters breach (4.9M vs 42M records — an unresolved disclosure-integrity question); Rutledge sold ~97% of his stake; zero insider buying through six months of drawdown. Escalation items are kill-switches, not vetoes.
- **ESG**: LAGGARD. $306.7M cumulative penalties, dominated by consumer protection ($243.5M) and disclosure failures (SEC $25M accounting-fraud penalty 2023; $144M securities settlement). Treat as a 0.5–1.0x turn multiple de-rating factor, not a standalone thesis.
- **Alternative Data**: Neutral with modest constructive tilt (low-medium confidence). Capitulation-reversal: +35% off the 26-Oct low on elevated volume; Spectrum/Xfinity search ratio 1.0x → 4.5x. But demand signals are flat, not inflecting — deterioration may be slowing; there is no turn yet.
- **Short / Contrarian View**: NO EDGE. "A broken business at a broken-business price." No fraud signature (Beneish −2.65, negative accruals four years running, 3.2x cash conversion) — removes the violent-short catalyst. The asymmetry has migrated to the credit, not the equity. Gross-margin "expansion" exposed as a $3.6B COGS→SG&A reclassification; true EBITDA margin flat for five years.

---

**Bull Case**
- **Deep value with dated catalysts**: ~4.8x EV/EBITDA, ~23% FCF yield; capex ≤$11B in 2027 + $2–3B cost-out takes PF FCF toward $9–11B — ~7–9% of net debt retired annually and a violent re-rating off a ~$21B cap.
- **Asymmetric rate optionality**: a 90bp drop in the 10Y (5.13% → ~4.25%) historically delivers a 0.7–1.0x cable multiple re-rating — worth +85–120% on this levered stub. HY spreads at 320bp keep refi access open.
- **Positioning washed out**: −76% peak-to-trough, then +35% off the low on rising volume; sector-best margins, mobile lines +15%, and zero geopolitical exposure.

**Bear Case**
- **Structural decline, accelerating**: pro forma internet −233k in Q3'26 (vs −171k a year ago), revenue −1.5%, EBITDA −4%, residential ARPU −1.8%. FWA and fiber are permanent share-takers; the $6.33B impairment is management's own admission.
- **Leverage into decline**: 3.93x, FCF/interest 1.2x, tangible equity −$77B. The bear case is not a drawdown — scenario value $0–40.
- **Governance/execution**: interim CFO through the largest integration in company history; $35B of buybacks at $300–500 average prices; a second impairment on the $97.6B goodwill/intangible balance is plausible.

**Key Risks**
CFO vacancy unresolved past ~Apr-2027 (control-environment failure); second franchise impairment; 2027 capex guided above $13B (kills the FCF thesis); leverage >4.25x (S&P downgrade trigger); ACP clawback or new securities filings; state rate regulation spreading beyond NY/CA; DSO >27 days (revenue quality); 10Y sustained above 5%.

**Agent disagreement flag**: The split is mandate-dependent, not factual — every agent agrees on the five core facts (accelerating sub losses, −1.5% revenue, ~3.9–4.6x leverage, impairment, cheapest large-cap telecom). Quality/trajectory agents (Growth, Sector, Macro, Risk) grade the business negatively; price/positioning agents (Value, Quant-value, Alt Data, Short) grade the price constructively. **Data gaps flagged**: post-deal share count unresolved (~145–167M; multiples carry ±30% uncertainty); 10-K/10-Q body, DEF 14A, and debt maturity ladder unretrievable; all four conflicts (share count, net debt, gross margin, revisions) adjudicated by the Portfolio Strategist and noted.

---

**Portfolio Construction Note** (Portfolio Strategist)

**Initiate 1.0% starter now; 2.5% maximum; telecom/cable sleeve hard cap 8%.** Kelly (55%) heavily discounted for parameter uncertainty, the 6.1x leverage multiplier, and governance overhang. Scale in 40/30/30: tranche 2 on pullback ≤$118 or a clean 29-Jan print; tranche 3 only on two consecutive quarters of improving pro forma net adds *and* 2027 capex guide ≤$11B. **Check CMCSA overlap first** (correlation 0.74 — a CHTR add is largely a duplicate cable bet); do not hold alongside a duration overweight — this is functionally a levered long-duration bond. Stops: halve on weekly close <$100, exit <$92. Fundamental kill-switches: Q4 internet losses >250k, leverage target abandoned, capex >$13B, second impairment, no permanent CFO by ~Apr-27, any enforcement/clawback event. Trim one-third at $205–215, another at $250 or EV/EBITDA >7.0x.

*One-liner for the PM: buy a small piece of a cheap, broken, levered franchise where the four remaining ways it becomes a permanent loss are each individually falsifiable before the position ever reaches full size.*

# PORTFOLIO CONSTRUCTION RECOMMENDATION — CHTR (Charter Communications)

**Decision date:** 13-Nov-2026 close · **Verified price: $138.39** (confirmed via daily OHLCV; the Short Analyst's $111.49 was the 30-Oct close — stale, and this matters because the stock is **+35% off the 26-Oct low of $102.18 in 13 sessions**)

Four conflicts had to be adjudicated because they drive the multiples:

| Conflict | Ruling |

Also unverified across the file: **10-K risk factors, 10-Q legal proceedings, DEF 14A, and the debt maturity ladder all failed retrieval (403s)**. Board independence, revenue-by-geography, and annual 2028–32 maturities are assumptions, not facts.

---

## 1. Agent Conviction Summary

| Agent | View | Conviction | Key Finding |
|---|---|---|---|
| **Sector Researcher** | Negative | High | Sector **UNATTRACTIVE**; company AVERAGE asset / negative momentum. Only peer with negative 2025 revenue (−0.6%), but **highest operating margin (24.4%, +320bp vs median)** and still improving. Ex-growth. |

| **Short Analyst** | **No edge** | Medium-High | "Bear case correct but fully discounted. Charter at $111 is a broken business at a broken-business price." **No fraud** (Beneish −2.65, negative accruals). Edge has migrated to the **credit**, not the equity. |

| **Portfolio Strategist** | **Initiate, small** | Medium | Value is real; leverage and governance cap the size, not the thesis. |

---

## 2. Consensus Assessment: **SPLIT** — but not in the way it looks

This is **not a genuine disagreement about facts**. Every agent agrees on the same five data points: (1) broadband units are falling and accelerating; (2) pro-forma revenue −1.5%, EBITDA −4%; (3) leverage ~3.9–4.6x with negative tangible equity; (4) $6.33B impairment; (5) the equity is optically the cheapest large-cap telecom asset in the US.

**The split is entirely mandate-dependent:**

- **Fundamental / risk agents (Sector, Growth, FinRisk, NonFinRisk, Macro, ESG) → negative.** They are grading *business quality and trajectory*. On that axis CHTR is unambiguously bad and getting worse.
- **Price / positioning agents (Value, Quant-value, Alt Data, Short) → constructive.** They are grading *price versus a non-apocalyptic outcome*. On that axis CHTR is unambiguously cheap.

**Two conflicts I am explicitly resolving:**

**(a) Value's $230–240 IV is too high — I haircut it to ~$195–215.** Value's base case needs EBITDA of ~$25.5B in 2028 at a **6.5x exit multiple**. Pro-forma EBITDA is *currently declining 4% YoY* and the deleveraging plan *requires* EBITDA growth. A base case that assumes the inflection it is supposed to be testing is not a base case; it is a bull case. Probability-weighting my own: **bear 30% ($15–40), base 45% (~$200), bull 25% (~$420) → ≈$208**, still **+50%** vs $138. The discount survives the haircut. It does not survive a 30% bear weight *and* a wipeout — which is why size, not the thesis, is the binding constraint.

**(b) Governance/fraud override does NOT trigger.** My framework says fraud or governance findings outrank a value call. Here the fraud case is **explicitly absent** — Short Analyst ran Beneish (−2.65), accruals (−0.072, negative four years running), and cash conversion (3.22x) and found clean accounting. Nonfin's concerns are **execution and disclosure quality, not fabrication**. That converts a veto into a *sizing haircut*. But Nonfin's escalation items 1–3 (CFO vacancy, impairment-vs-underwriting reconciliation, cyber disclosure adequacy) are **unresolved and must be monitored as explicit kill-switches** (see §6).

**Agreement level: SPLIT (high agreement on facts, low agreement on action).** The only true two-sided risk in the file is **timing** — Value wants it now, Growth wants it after two clean quarters. I side with neither: scale in.

---

## 3. Position Sizing Recommendation: **1.0% now, 2.5% maximum**

**Kelly logic, then heavily haircut:**

| Input | Value |
|---|---|
| Expected value | ~$208 (+50%) |
| Win probability | ~70% |
| Avg win / avg loss | ~+150% / −75% → payoff ratio b ≈ 2.0 |
| Full Kelly f = p − q/b | 0.70 − (0.30/2.0) = **0.55 (55%)** |

55% is obviously unusable — Kelly on a fat-tailed, binary, levered-equity outcome with a $0 floor produces nonsense. Apply the standard discounts:

- **÷4 for parameter uncertainty** (share count unknown ±30%, net debt three different figures, four primary filings unretrievable, PT dispersion $19.30–$66.34 on FY27 EPS) → ~14%
- **÷3 for the 59% vol / 6.1x leverage multiplier** — position *risk contribution*, not weight, is the constraint. A 1.5% weight at 4x market volatility contributes ~6% of portfolio risk.
- **×0.7 for governance overhang** (interim CFO, $6.3B impairment, live investigations)

→ **Max position: 2.5% of portfolio. Starter today: 1.0%.**

**Rationale in one line:** the asymmetry is genuinely exceptional (5:1 up/down skew from here), but the bear case is a **permanent capital loss, not a drawdown**, the CFO seat is empty, and the entry has already improved 35% in two weeks. A 1.0% starter buys the optionality at a size where a total wipeout costs 100bp and a double adds 100bp — genuinely symmetric in *portfolio* terms even though it is 5:1 in *security* terms.

**Not sized larger, explicitly, because:** (i) at $102 two weeks ago this was a 2.5–3% position — the +35% move has already consumed a third of the margin of safety; (ii) conviction here is *medium*, not high, and my framework caps medium-conviction-plus-multiple-risk-flags at 1–3%.

---

## 4. Portfolio Fit Analysis

**Sector concentration — CAUTION.** Communication Services is rated **UNATTRACTIVE** by the Sector Researcher. But note the composition: the sector's +6.7% growth is entirely Alphabet/Meta/Netflix. Buying CHTR adds exposure to the **telecom/cable sub-segment growing 0–3%**, which is the *worst* part of an already-unattractive sector. **Hard rule: total telecom/cable sleeve (CHTR + CMCSA + VZ + T + TMUS) must not exceed 8% of portfolio.** If the portfolio is already at that cap, funding must come from VZ or T — and that is a downgrade in credit quality, which is the wrong trade.

**Correlation — the most important number in this report:**

| Pair | 252d correlation |
|---|---|
| **CHTR – CMCSA** | **0.742** ← critical |
| CHTR – VZ | 0.357 |
| CHTR – T | 0.341 |
| CHTR – TMUS | 0.263 |
| CHTR – SPY | **−0.029** |

The Quant Analyst called CHTR "almost pure idiosyncratic risk." **That is wrong for portfolio purposes.** CHTR is 0.74 correlated with Comcast — the highest pair in the entire peer matrix outside the VZ/T pair (0.82). **If this portfolio owns CMCSA, a CHTR position is largely a duplicate cable bet, not a diversifier.** Check CMCSA first. If CMCSA >2%, either fund CHTR out of CMCSA or halve the CHTR starter.

The **−0.03 correlation to SPY is a trap, not a gift.** R² = 0.0009; the beta is statistically meaningless (t ≈ 0.48). Do not count CHTR toward equity-market diversification or as a hedge. Its true factors are **credit spreads, long-duration rates, and broadband net adds**.

**Factor exposure.** This position adds: **deep value (95th pct)**, **severe negative momentum (5th pct)**, **high volatility (3rd pct)**, **average quality (60th)**. Net effect: increases the portfolio's value tilt and its realized volatility. It is *not* a low-vol or defensive add despite the "cable utility" label — realized vol 59% vs 26% for VZ.

**Hidden rate duration — the real portfolio risk.** The Macro Researcher's math is the clearest thing in the file: on ~$126B EV, a 0.7–1.0x multiple re-rating from a 90bp drop in the 10Y is worth **$16–23B against a ~$22B market cap**. **This position is functionally a levered long-duration bond.** If the portfolio is already long duration (long TLT, utilities, REITs, growth equity), buying CHTR doubles an existing bet. **Do not own this alongside a duration overweight.**

**Recommended pairing:** Short Analyst's structure is the professionally correct one for a risk-budget-conscious book — **long VZ/T, short CHTR** captures the relative-decline thesis with no squeeze risk. I am not recommending it as the primary expression because the equity's downside is now largely priced, but it is the right *hedge* if the 2.5% max is reached.

---

## 5. Entry Strategy: **Scale in — 40 / 30 / 30**

Do **not** take full size at $138.39.

| Tranche | Size | Trigger | Rationale |
|---|---|---|---|
| **1 (now)** | 1.0% of portfolio | Market, $138.39 | Establishes the option. Buys the asymmetry. |
| **2** | +0.75% | Pullback ≤$118 **OR** the 29-Jan-27 Q4 print passes cleanly | $118 is where the post-Q3 reversal began; gives back ~15% of the recent rip |
| **3** | +0.75% | Two consecutive quarters of improving pro-forma internet net adds **AND** 2027 capex guide ≤$11B | This is Growth Researcher's exact "revisit" condition. Do not skip it. |

**Why not all at once:** the next print is **29-Jan-2027** (EPS est $9.51, −8% YoY) with a **28.6% historical beat rate** and a tape that gapped **−25.5% in one session on 24-Apr-26** and −18.6% on 25-Jul-25. Size tranche 1 so that a −25% gap event costs **≤25bp of portfolio**. Volume confirms the fragility: 6.5M shares on 6-Nov, 4.4M on 10-Nov, against ~2.5M normal ADV.

**Why not wait entirely:** the Short Analyst's strongest point — "the bear case is told" — plus the +17% post-Q3 reversal on rising volume means the cost of waiting is real. If the 10Y breaks to 4.5%, this is a $220 stock and the entry is gone. Tranche 1 is the price of admission for having a view at all.

---

## 6. Risk Management Rules

**Price stop (mechanical, secondary — this is a fundamental position, not a momentum one):**
- Weekly close below **$100** (beneath the 26-Oct low of $101.11) → **halve the position**
- Hard stop **$92** → exit remaining. A break of the post-impairment low with no new information means the market is pricing something the file does not contain.

**Thesis invalidation — exit on ANY of these (fundamental, primary):**

1. **Q4'26 pro-forma internet losses > 250k** (i.e., worse than the 233k already reported). The trend line is the whole thesis: −120k → −172k → −233k must break.
2. **Leverage target abandoned, or net leverage > 4.25x.** 4.25x is S&P's tightened post-Cox downgrade threshold — crossing it is a credit event, not a sentiment event.
3. **2027 capex guided above $13B.** This breaks the entire FCF-inflection thesis. The value case has no other leg.
4. **Second franchise/goodwill impairment.** One on a $97.6B balance that is 63% of assets is an admission; two is a pattern. Cut to one-third.
5. **A permanent CFO not named by ~30-Apr-2027.** Nonfin's item 1: six months of interim finance leadership through the largest integration in company history is a control-environment failure. This is the cleanest single governance kill-switch in the file.
6. **Any of: FCC/DOJ/SEC enforcement action · ACP subsidy clawback notice · a new securities class action tied to the Q3'26 impairment · a cyber 8-K Item 1.05 disclosure gap confirmed.** Any one of these converts "high risk" to "uninvestable at any size."
7. **DSO climbing past 27 days** (currently 24.5, from 19.8). Short Analyst's loudest unresolved flag — if it is collections rather than mobile handset receivables, revenue quality is misrepresented.

**Trim trigger:** trim one-third at **$205–215** (~90% of my haircut intrinsic value), another third at **$250**, or at **EV/EBITDA > 7.0x**, whichever comes first. Do not hold for the full bull case — on a 6.1x leverage multiplier, giving back the re-rating is the entire risk.

**Rebalance trigger:** if CHTR exceeds 3.5% of portfolio on price appreciation alone, trim back to 2.5%.

---

## 7. Final Portfolio Action: **INITIATE — STARTER POSITION, 1.0%**

**Not Pass**, because: the ~50% discount to a *haircut* intrinsic value is real; the bear case is priced; there is no fraud; the FCF inflection from capex ≤$11B plus $2–3B of cost-out is a dated, verifiable catalyst; and the sector's cleanest geopolitical profile removes one whole risk category.

**Starter size: 1.0% of portfolio. Maximum: 2.5%. Hard ceiling on the telecom/cable sleeve: 8%.**

## SECTOR BRIEF — Charter Communications (CHTR)
### Sector: Communication Services / US Cable & Fixed Broadband | Date: ~13 Nov 2026

---

### 1. Sector Overview

Charter competes in US cable/fixed broadband, a ~$64bn revenue market (US fixed broadband, 2025) that is now **structurally mature and shrinking in units even as it grows in dollars**. The domestic market is highly concentrated — Comcast (~$124bn), Charter (~$55bn standalone, ~$60bn+ pro forma post-Cox) and AT&T (~$126bn) control the large majority of residential broadband, giving a de facto oligopoly with an HHI well above 2,500 — yet the emergence of 5G fixed wireless access (FWA) as a genuine third pipe from Verizon, T-Mobile and AT&T has raised effective rivalry sharply without adding new fixed infrastructure. Sector revenue growth across the top-10 Communication Services names was **+6.7% in 2025** ($1,900.7bn → $2,027.1bn), but that is almost entirely Alphabet/Meta/Netflix-driven; **telecom and cable sub-segments grew 0–3%**, and the aggregated gross margin slipped from 57.6% to 54.4%. Charter's own trajectory captures the cycle: revenue growth decelerated from **+7.5% (2021) → +4.5% → +1.1% → +0.9% → −0.6% (2025)**, and pro forma (incl. Cox) Q3'26 revenue fell **1.5% YoY**. This is a late-cycle, ex-growth sector in the classic sense: penetration near saturation, pricing power eroding, capital intensity high, and returns now driven by cost extraction and balance-sheet management rather than volume.

---

### 2. Key Tailwinds

- **Consolidation-driven cost synergies and scale.** The Cox + Liberty Broadband closings (19 Aug 2026) added **11m passings and 5m customers**, and management targets **$2.0bn of incremental annualised run-rate opex savings over 18 months** — roughly 3.6% of revenue, a meaningful offset to a −1% top line. National scale also strengthens content/programming negotiating leverage.
- **Converged mobile bundling is the growth engine.** Mobile lines are growing even where broadband is not (legacy Cox added **70k mobile lines** in Q3'26 alone), lifting revenue per household and reducing churn. Charter's MVNO economics improve with volume, and wireless bundling is now the primary retention tool against FWA.
- **Deleveraging and FCF-driven re-rating potential.** Management targets **3.5x net leverage within three years**; post-Cox the equity is priced for financial distress (see §5), so any credible path to deleveraging plus a stabilising broadband base creates asymmetric optionality. BEAD's **$42.45bn** federal program also subsidises rural edge-out that cable can serve opportunistically.

### 3. Key Headwinds

- **Leverage and impairment risk.** Charter carries ~4.5x gross leverage; Q3'26 included a **$6.3bn impairment charge** driving a **$2.1–2.4bn net loss** (~$20.50/share). ### 5. Target Company's Competitive Position: **AVERAGE** (strong asset, weak momentum)

**Why not "strong":** Charter's asset base is genuinely best-in-class — the largest US cable footprint post-Cox (~32m customers, 41 states), sector-leading operating margins, and a fully-owned network that FWA operators must rent spectrum to match. On a pure cost-to-serve and margin basis it is the most efficient operator in the peer set. That is a durable, hard-to-replicate advantage: barriers to entry in fixed broadband remain high (capital intensity, right-of-way, decades of plant), and no rational entrant is building a third national wireline network.

**Why not "weak":** Momentum and financial flexibility are the weak link. Charter is the only major peer with contracting revenue, is losing broadband units to FWA and fiber, carries the sector's most strained balance sheet relative to its shrinking equity base, and has just taken a $6.3bn impairment. The Cox deal buys scale and cost synergies but was struck at a moment of maximum weakness for cable equity, and integration risk is real.

Net: a structurally advantaged franchise currently earning below its cost of capital on new broadband investment, trading as a distressed credit proxy. **Average, with negative momentum** — the operational fix (cost-out + bundling) is credible but unproven, and the terminal-value debate on fixed broadband is unresolved.

## 2. Top 3 Geopolitical / Policy Risks

**Risk 1 — U.S. rate regulation spreads beyond New York (Probability: High | Impact: Medium-High)**
New York's Affordable Broadband Act ($15/mo for 25 Mbps; $20/mo for 200 Mbps) took effect Jan 2025 after the **Supreme Court declined to disturb** the lower-court ruling (Broadband Breakfast; Digital Inclusion, 2026). Charter now markets a "$15/mo" NY tier (Spectrum Internet Assist). This is the single most important precedent in U.S. broadband: it establishes that a state PUC can set retail rates for a cable ISP. The Cox merger approvals **added further price-like conditions** — CPUC required Lifeline service tiers for five years, honoring "price-for-life" contracts, automatic outage bill credits, and free service to schools/libraries/community centers (CPUC Commissioner Baker, 12 Aug 2026, via CAGW). **Risk 2 — Federal merger conditions have converted the FCC into a de facto operating partner (Probability: Certain | Impact: Medium)**
The FCC approved Charter/Cox on 27 Feb 2026 only after Charter agreed to: (i) **eliminate DEI policies and workforce diversity targets**; (ii) **onshore all Cox offshore job functions within 18 months**; (iii) a minimum starting wage commitment; and (iv) rural buildout (FCC DOC-419093A1; Fierce Network, 2 Mar 2026). ## 1. Credit Risk Assessment — **Sub-Investment Grade (BB+/Ba1), high-quality HY, deteriorating**

Charter sits **one notch below investment grade** (S&P 'BB+' affirmed Aug-2026; Fitch 'BB+'; Moody's 'Ba1' senior secured). The IG upgrade thesis has stalled: management closed the **Cox Communications acquisition on 19-Aug-2026** (advancing 11M+ passings, 5M+ customer relationships), which levered the balance sheet back up to **3.93x net debt/EBITDA versus a 3.5x target** (~$104B net debt on ~$26.4B annualized pro forma Adjusted EBITDA).

The credit is **not** covenant-fragile — HY indentures of this type are incurrence-based, not maintenance-based, so a bad quarter does not trigger default. The real risk is **structural decline plus refinancing cost**, not a technical breach.

**Service capacity is adequate but thin relative to the balance sheet:**
- Annualized cash interest **$5.8B** against $26.4B PF Adj. EBITDA = **4.55x EBITDA/interest**.
- But EBIT coverage is only **~2.7x** on $15.8B EBIT ($26.4B EBITDA less ~$10.6B PF D&A). FY2025 as-reported coverage was **2.65x** (operating income $13.34B / interest $5.04B), or **2.48x** on EBIT.
- Free cash flow covers interest just **~1.2x** ($7.0B PF FCF / $5.8B interest). That is the tightest of the coverage measures and the one to watch.
- Weighted average cost of debt **5.3%** vs. a **5.13% 10Y Treasury** and a non-inverted curve (2Y 4.74%, 30Y 5.47%). Charter is refinancing at approximately its existing coupon — no rate tailwind, no acute shock.

**The equity cushion is the weakness.** Book equity $20.5B (13% of assets) against $97.1B YE2025 debt, of which **goodwill + intangibles = $97.6B (63% of total assets)** → **tangible book equity is approximately –$77B**. Retained earnings are a **–$5.4B deficit**. Equity is a thin, option-like claim: each 1.0x turn of EV/EBITDA on $26.4B of EBITDA moves equity value by ~$26B — roughly **140% of the entire market cap**.

**Altman Z-Score 0.60 (Distress zone)** — I treat this as directionally, not literally, informative. The model was built for manufacturers and is systematically biased against goodwill-heavy, negative-working-capital cable operators (X1 = –0.053 from working capital, X2 = –0.035 from the retained deficit, X4 = 0.15 on book equity / 0.14 on market cap). Only X3 (0.081) and X5 (0.355) contribute. That said, a 0.60 reading vs. a 2.99 safe-zone threshold correctly captures a **very thin equity buffer**.

**Piotroski F-Score 7/9 (Moderate-to-strong)** is the counterweight: positive ROA, positive operating cash flow, good accruals quality, lower leverage, no dilution, gross margin expansion. Misses on ROA improvement and asset turnover. Financial *direction* of the legacy business is not yet broken — the Cox consolidation clouds the forward read.
